title: Platelet count

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A platelet count measures the number of platelets in your blood. Platelets are small blood cells that stick together to help form blood clots and slow or stop bleeding.
context: A platelet count is often part of a complete blood count done at a regular checkup. It is most often used to look at conditions that cause too much bleeding or clotting, and your provider reviews it with your symptoms and other tests.
aboveRange: Can be associated with inflammatory bowel conditions such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, or rheumatoid arthritis
Can be associated with certain cancers such as lung cancer or breast cancer
belowRange: A viral infection such as mononucleosis, hepatitis, or measles
Gestational thrombocytopenia, a common and mild low-platelet condition during pregnancy that usually gets better on its own
Vitamin B12 deficiency, or an autoimmune condition
Can be associated with cirrhosis, bone marrow conditions, leukemia, or lymphoma
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
